k1941:
A studio at Plazh Hekurudha with something few flats of its size have: an entrance of its own.

The certificate records 47.15 m², laid out as a living room with the kitchen, on the first residential floor. At that area the space is closer to a small flat than to the usual studio.

The private entrance is the point. It means coming and going without the shared stairwell, which matters for anyone letting short-term, and it gives the flat a degree of independence that a door off a landing does not.

The paperwork is in order, and this is one of the more sought-after parts of Plazh.
k1942: 756 m² building plot at Shkozet, Durrës
k1943: A 756 m² plot at Shkozet, in a developed part of Durrës with room for building or a business project.
k1944:
A building plot of 756 m² at Shkozet, in a part of Durrës that has already been built up around it.

The size is the useful thing here. Seven hundred square metres is enough to plan a building properly rather than fit one into what is left, and enough to leave ground around whatever goes up.

Shkozet sits between the city and the motorway, which makes it as workable for a business project as for a house.

Nothing stands on the land at present, so the use is a matter for the buyer and the planning rules.
k1945: 1+1 apartments with garages in Liburna Residence, Golem
k1946: One-bedroom flats of about 71 to 74 m² in Liburna Residence, seventy metres from the sea, with private garages available.
k1947:
One-bedroom apartments in Building 1A of Liburna Residence at Golem, seventy metres from the sea.

Each is laid out the same way: a living room with a kitchen corner, a bedroom, a bathroom and a balcony, with total areas running from about 71 to 74 m².

The floor decides the price. Units on the first floor are offered at the lower rate; those on the sixth and topmost floor carry a sea view and a correspondingly higher rate per square metre. Which of those is worth paying for depends entirely on whether the flat is meant to be lived in or let.

Four private garages sit in the basement with their own entrance, and a garage can be bought together with an apartment. The building is finished to a high standard, with thermal and acoustic insulation, and the promenade and beach are a short walk away.
k1948: Studio in a new building with a lift, Plepa
k1949: A 40 m² studio on the third floor of a new building at Plepa, with a lift; the price is open to discussion.
k1950:
A studio at Plepa, in a recently built block with a lift.

The total area is 40 m² with 35.2 m² net, on the third floor above the ground.

Being in a new building matters more at this size than at any other: the services and finishes are current, and a small flat has nowhere to hide an old bathroom or tired wiring.

Plepa is a settled residential area with the everyday services close at hand. It works as a first purchase or as a flat held and let, and the seller will discuss the price.
k1951: 2+1 apartment with a balcony near the hospital, Durrës
k1952: An 80 m² two-bedroom flat with a balcony on the third floor, in a settled part of Durrës near the hospital.
k1953:
A 2+1 apartment near the hospital in Durrës, on the third floor.

The flat measures 80 m²: two bedrooms, a living room with the kitchen, a bathroom and a balcony. The plan is practical — the rooms are proportioned to be used rather than admired.

The quarter around it is lived in rather than newly built, with the everyday services already where they are needed and good access across the city.

At this size and this position it works equally as a family home and as something bought to let.
k1954: Five-storey business building in the centre of Durrës
k1955: A 701 m² commercial building in central Durrës: two shops at street level, three floors of offices and a bar-café with a loft on top.
k1956:
A five-storey commercial building in one of the busiest parts of central Durrës, sold as a whole.

The total area is 701 m² with 568 m² net. The ground floor holds two shop units; three floors above are divided into fifteen offices; the top floor is a bar-café with a loft above it. There are eighteen lavatories across the building, and it has a lift.

The arrangement is already income-producing in shape: retail at street level where the footfall is, offices in the middle where they are cheapest to service, and hospitality at the top where the view is worth something.

The building is new and the mortgage paperwork is in order. Something of this size and mix is priced on application rather than on a list.
k1957: Front-line 1+1 apartment with a garage included, Shkëmbi i Kavajës
k1958: A 74 m² one-bedroom flat on the front line at Shkëmbi i Kavajës, with a 32 m² private garage included in the price.
k1959:
A 1+1 apartment on the front line at Shkëmbi i Kavajës, on the first residential floor of a residence that is managed and maintained all year round.

The flat measures 74 m² gross and 64 m² net: a living room with the kitchen, a bedroom, a bathroom and a balcony. It faces east, so the light comes early and the afternoon heat goes elsewhere.

A private garage of 32 m² comes with it and is included in the price, not offered alongside it. On this stretch in August, that is worth stating plainly.

The building has a lift and the mortgage paperwork is in order. Being on the front line with the sea in front is what sets this apart from the flats a street back.
k1960: Studio under construction 300 m from the sea, Golem

k1962:
A studio in a residential block being built at Golem, three hundred metres from the sea.

The internal area is 37.22 m², with a further 10.87 m² of shared space, on the ground floor of a six-storey building. Inside there is a living room, a bedroom and a bathroom.

Payment follows the build in four stages: two fifths on signing, then a further three tenths when the shell is finished, a fifth when plastering starts and the last tenth on handover of the keys.

One point to raise with the seller before anything else: the completion date originally given for this project has now passed, so the current handover date needs confirming in writing rather than assuming.

k1973: A ground-floor one-bedroom unit of 43.87 m² internal plus 11.89 m² shared, in a Golem block under construction; several identical units are available.
